set.hook: Family-run Southwest auberge by the church in La Môle, cash only, terrines brought in tubs to share.

set.hook: Bistrot de Pays in Ampus, 600 m up: daube, wood-fired pizza and dishes that follow the market.

set.hook: Toulon's morning food market along the Cours Lafayette, Tuesday to Sunday, 7:30 to 12:30.
set.why: Every morning but Monday the Cours Lafayette, on the edge of Toulon's old town, is lined for about a kilometre with stalls of Provençal growers, fishmongers, cheese and charcuterie, spilling into Place Louis Blanc. Gilbert Bécaud, born in Toulon in 1927, sang it in 1957 in Les marchés de Provence. In the afternoon a separate non-food market takes the same pavement, from 2:30 to 6:30.

set.hook: Collobrières chestnut confectioner since 1948, with a free museum of the old candying machines.
set.why: The Maures chestnut has been candied in Collobrières since 1948 at this house on the Boulevard Koenig, which makes marrons glacés, chestnut cream, chestnut ice cream and candied fruit. Alongside the shop, the Musée de la fabrique du marron glacé shows the tools and machines once used to sort, peel and candy the nuts, and entry is free. The village's chestnut festival runs on three Sundays, 11 to 25 October 2026.

houses.title: Three old houses, three kitchens
houses.story: The Var's old houses are inns and hotels that outlived the trade they were built for. Hôtel La Ponche began as a 1930s fishermen's bar on the Saint-Tropez cove of the same name; MICHELIN now lists its restaurant without a star, with Simon Pinault cooking the day's catch. The Auberge de la Môle has served Southwest France, foie gras and frogs' legs, to the coast since 1962, cash only, with its 2026 season listed as ending on 11 October. Le Pont d'Or in Barjols was a coaching inn and has been kept by one family for four generations; it opens from mid-January to the end of November and is known locally for a Friday aïoli.
houses.where: Hôtel La Ponche, Saint-Tropez; Auberge de la Môle, La Môle; Le Pont d'Or, Barjols

hautvar.title: Village tables of the Haut-Var
hautvar.story: Up in the Haut-Var the hill villages keep few tables, and each one counts for the village. In Ampus, at about 600 metres above the Nartuby gorges, the Auberge des Braconniers joined the Bistrot de Pays network in 2021, a label that asks for local producers; it serves daube next to wood-fired pizza. In Aups, which holds a black truffle market every January, Valentine Lorcher and Adrien Antelme opened Solea in 2024; Gault&Millau scores it 12.5/20. In Cotignac, Picotte, the southern branch of a Paris bistro opened in 2020, cooks southern regional dishes on rue Saint-Jean.
hautvar.where: L'Auberge des Braconniers, Ampus; Solea, Aups; Picotte Provence, Cotignac

maures.title: Forest villages and the Hyères road
maures.story: The Massif des Maures is chestnut and cork-oak country behind the coast, and its tables cook from it. In Collobrières, whose chestnut festival runs on three October Sundays in 2026, La Petite Fontaine serves daube, petits farcis and supions on a 34-euro menu. In the old village of Bormes, Lou Portaou is built into the vaulted passage of the ruelle des Sarrasins, held by Philippe Cavatore since 1986; the tourism office gives its 2026 season as February to August. On the Toulon road out of Hyères, Pascal and Nadège Bonamy have run La Colombe since 1987, year-round, with menus from 45 to 75 euros.
maures.where: La Petite Fontaine, Collobrières; Lou Portaou, Bormes-les-Mimosas; La Colombe, Hyères

domaines.title: Mourvèdre, marl and a Templar estate
domaines.story: Bandol's reds are built on Mourvèdre, a late-ripening grape that needs the sun and the sea air of this coast, and the Côtes de Provence inland make mostly rosé. Château de Pibarnon farms about 52 hectares organically on blue marl in a bowl of terraces above La Cadière; Gault&Millau gives its 2020 red 93/100. Domaine de Terrebrune in Ollioules ages its wine in galleries Georges Delille cut into Triassic rock after 1963, and offers a 15-euro visit. La Commanderie de Peyrassol, a Templar commandery from the 13th century, adds a sculpture park and Chez Jeannette, which kept its MICHELIN star in 2026.
domaines.where: Château de Pibarnon, La Cadière-d'Azur; Domaine de Terrebrune, Ollioules; La Commanderie de Peyrassol, Flassans-sur-Issole

street.title: Cade, market stalls, candied chestnuts
street.story: The Var's street food is cheap, made in the morning and sold standing up. Cade, a chickpea-flour galette thicker and softer than the socca of Nice, is Toulon's own, and La Cade à Dédé bakes it in a wood-fired oven on a trailer at the Cours Lafayette for about 2.50 euros a portion. The Cours Lafayette market itself, which Gilbert Bécaud sang in 1957, runs Tuesday to Sunday from 7:30 to 12:30 all year. Inland in Collobrières, the Confiserie Azuréenne has candied Maures chestnuts since 1948 and keeps a free museum of its old machines.
street.where: La Cade à Dédé, Toulon; Marché du Cours Lafayette, Toulon; Confiserie Azuréenne, Collobrières
